rationale: C14 is the strongest comparison because both are letters urging prompt favorable congressional action on an international measure and argue that action would demonstrate American leadership and resolve to the world. C10 similarly urges favorable committee action and treats enactment as a worldwide demonstration of democratic principles. C04 shares the United Nations, communist-victim, and fundamental-rights setting. These overlaps, however, remain general advocacy themes and routine legislative-letter structure. None supplies distinctive shared wording, a parallel sequence of concrete provisions, or reusable legal or administrative machinery material enough to support a drafting-template relationship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I sincerely hope that the Senate Foreign Relations Committee will report favorably on the Genocide Convention within the next few days
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I believe the Congress of the United States has an opportunity to strike a major blow for peace on behalf of people everywhere by taking rapid and favorable action on this legislation.
shared_material.explanation: C14 shares the request for prompt favorable congressional action on an international measure, but this is conventional advocacy language rather than distinctive borrowing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: we will let the world know that the United States does not condone mass atrocities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It will be tangible evidence of our determination to achieve this kind of peace--evidence which will be understood by every nation in the world.
shared_material.explanation: C14 uses a similar argument that enactment will signal American resolve internationally, but the formulation and substantive measure differ.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This tragic situation brings out the need for the free and civilized nations of the world to cooperate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: These are troubled times. I know of few better ways in which we can demonstrate to the world our deep faith in democracy and the principles of self-government
shared_material.explanation: C10 has comparable world-facing democratic rhetoric, but no distinctive language or common operative structure establishes templating.
